Application Materials.content:
Please upload these supporting documents as a PDF onto the [Graduate Admission System](https://gradapp.nus.edu.sg/portal/app_manage). The total size of your uploaded documents should not exceed 10MB. Documents not in English must be accompanied with certified copies of the English-translated version. Incomplete applications will not be considered. **You do not need to mail us any documents during the application stage.** **Letters of recommendation, reference letters and referee details are not required to be submitted.**
| | Supporting document | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Your resume | Your updated resume detailing your educational background, internship and work experience (if any), achievements, etc. |
| 2 | Copy of your official identification documents | Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents: A copy of your NRIC (front and back). International applicants: A copy of your passport (identification page). |
| 3 | Certified copies of your transcripts/mark sheets and degree certificate | Official transcripts and attested copy of degree scroll will be required after you are offered a place in the programme. Transcript Request Forms are available via this [link](https://bschool.nus.edu.sg/msc-accounting-qat/wp-content/uploads/sites/120/2023/09/Transcript-Request-Form.pdf). |
| 4 | A Letter of Motivation | _Not more than 500 words_. |
| 6 | GMAT/GRE scores (optional) | **GMAT:** Please designate **“National University of Singapore” (GMAT Code: DRT-MK-51 MSc in Accounting and Financial Analytics)** as your score recipient. **GRE:** Please designate **“4642 – NUS Business School MSc Programmes”** as your score recipient. |
| 7 | TOEFL / IELTS scores (if applicable) | **IELTS**: Please upload a softcopy of your IELTS Test Report Form via the application portal. **TOEFL**: Please upload a softcopy of your TOEFL Score Report via the application portal and indicate the institution code – “0677 National University of Singapore”. |
If you are offered admission, official transcripts must be sent by the institution / university in a sealed envelope with its flap bearing the security seal of the institution / university directly to: MSc Programmes Office, Mochtar Riady Building Level 2, 15 Kent Ridge Drive, Singapore 119245.

Interview Requirements.content: A strong performance in the interview (conducted for shortlisted candidates only).

Application Deadlines.content:
There is only one intake in August each year for the [MSc in Accounting and Financial Analytics programme](https://mscacc.nus.edu.sg/).
The key application dates for the August 2026 intake are:
| Date | Event |
| --- | --- |
| **1 September 2025** | Application opens |
| **15 November 2025*** | Cut-off date for 1st round of application; Cut-off date for study award consideration |
| **15 February 2026*** | Application deadline for all applicants |
| By June 2026 | Notification of application outcome for all applicants |
| Late July 2026 | Orientation and Commencement of Classes |
*Applications received on or before each cut-off date will be reviewed after the respective deadline. Admission offers for the first cut-off will be issued on a rolling basis commencing in January/February and for the second cut-off commencing in March/April. All applicants will be notified of their outcomes no later than July.
Please note that applications will only be reviewed if both the **application form is submitted** and the **application fee is paid** by the specified deadlines. Additionally, applications are valid for the immediate upcoming intake only.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **Educational Background:** A good undergraduate degree in any discipline. Applicants in the process of earning a degree or about to graduate are welcome to apply.
- **Work Experience:** We do not require you to have work experience for admission into the programme. Applicants with some postgraduate work experience are also welcome to apply.

GRE GMAT Requirements.content:
GMAT/GRE is optional. You are also welcome to submit an application without a GMAT/GRE score. A strong score may enhance your application. Generally, a score of **700 out of 800 for the GMAT**, or the GMAT equivalent in GRE is expected. However, as it is not mandatory, you are also welcome to submit an application without a GMAT/GRE score.
A GMAT score is highly recommended if your GPA is not strong. Applicants with lower GPAs are encouraged to strengthen their application with a competitive GRE or GMAT score.
For GMAT, please visit the [official GMAT website](https://www.mba.com/exams/gmat). Please designate “**National University of Singapore” GMAT Code: DRT-MK-51 (MSc in Accounting and Financial Analytics)** as your GMAT score recipient. For GRE, please visit the [official GRE website](https://www.ets.org/gre/?WT.ac=etshome_gre_menu_180417). Please designate “**4642 – NUS Business School MSc Programmes**” as your GRE score recipient.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
#### **English Language Requirement**
If English is not the native language or medium of prior undergraduate instruction. For **TOEFL**, the internet-based test score must be at least **5.0**. For **IELTS**, the overall band score must be at least **7.0**.

Program Overview.content:
Explore the NUS Master of Science in Accounting and Financial Analytics, tailored to empower graduates in navigating the evolving landscape of the accounting industry and insights to thrive in a data-driven world. With increased adoption of technology, accounting firms now face new demands to recruit employees who possess data analytics skills combined with accounting knowledge. Our programmes integrates cutting-edge technology with traditional accounting principles, providing essential skills.
NUS Business School offers the MSc in Accounting and Financial Analytics degree as a trend-setting programme designed to transform you — a graduate with a first degree in any discipline — into an individual who is ready to take on the opportunities and challenges of the new digital world. An MSc in Accounting and Financial Analytics graduate, equipped with a blend of accounting and data analytics skills, can either rise as a more finance-savvy executive within the same organisation or branch out into new roles not previously thought possible, such as an auditor, data analyst, equity analyst, M&A advisor, or even an entrepreneur.
**Industries our graduates work in**
Our MACC graduates are hired across a wide range of industries such as:
- Accounting & Audit Services
- Information Communications & Technology
- Banking & Financial Services
- Pharmaceutical, Healthcare, Biomedical Sciences
- Public Sector
- Distribution, Logistics & Supply Chain
- Agriculture & Commodity trade
Our MACC graduates are involved in job functions such as:
- Auditor
- Assistant Accountant
- Financial Analyst
- Fixed Income & Currencies Analyst
- M&A Advisor
- Tax Specialist
- Trust Manager
- Management Associate

Curriculum.content:
**12 Months. 40 Units.** The [MSc in Accounting and Financial Analytics (MACC)](https://mscacc.nus.edu.sg/) programme is delivered intensively over 12 months in a three-semester structure that includes experiential learning in the final semester. Please [click here](https://www.nus.edu.sg/registrar/calendar) for the NUS Academic Calendar.
| Semester 1 | Semester 2 | Special Term |
|---|---|---|
| Aug - Nov | Jan - Apr | May - Jul/May - Nov |
| 4 Core Courses (16 Units) **OR** 4 Core Courses (16 Units) + 1 Elective Course (4 Units) | 2 Core Courses (8 Units) + 3 Elective Courses (12 Units) **OR** 2 Core Courses (8 Units) + 2 Elective Courses (8 Units) | Experiential Learning (4 Units) |
Full Course = 4 units (3 hours/week, 13 weeks duration).
Core courses:
- Semester 1: Applied Data Science & Visualisation; Corporate Valuations Models; Managerial Planning and Control; Preparing Financial Statements.
- Semester 2: Analytics & Data Management; Corporate Accounting and Reporting.
Elective courses:
- Semester 1: Taxes and Business Strategy.
- Semester 2: Bank Compliance and Risk Management; Financial Statement Analysis; Mergers and Acquisitions; Audit Analytics and Business Intelligence.
Special Term:
- Experiential Learning: Through an industry internship or applied project, students engage in experiential learning by analysing and solving problems faced by professionals in the accounting field. These internships and applied projects are primarily self-sourced.
To graduate from the NUS MSc in Accounting and Financial Analytics programme, students must complete the programme requirements and achieve a Grade Point Average (GPA) of at least **3.2 out of 5.0**. To stay and complete the programme, students must maintain a GPA of at least **3.2**.

Cost of Attendance.content:
Studying in Singapore as an international student requires careful budgeting, as monthly living costs can vary depending on your lifestyle, accommodation choice, and daily spending habits. The estimated monthly living expenses for an international student living in Singapore can look like this:
| Category | Budget Student Lifestyle | Typical Student Lifestyle | More Comfortable Lifestyle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Accommodation | S$500-S$800 | S$1,000-S$1,500 | S$2,400-S$3,500 |
| Food | S$250-S$350 | S$350-S$500 | S$500-S$700 |
| Transportation | S$80-S$130 | S$100-S$180 | S$150-S$250 |
| Utilities | S$30-S$60 | S$30-S$60 | S$40-S$80 |
| Mobile Phone Plan | S$15-S$30 | S$15-S$30 | S$20-S$40 |
| Internet | S$0-S$20 | S$20-S$40 | S$30-S$60 |
| Dining Out | S$100-S$200 | S$200-S$300 | S$300-S$400 |
| Entertainment | S$20-S$40 | S$40-S$60 | S$40-S$80 |
| Fitness and Sports | S$0-S$15 | S$15-S$30 | S$80-S$150 |
| Personal Care and Shopping | S$20-S$40 | S$40-S$80 | S$60-S$120 |
| Estimated Monthly Total | ~S$1,000-S$1,700 | ~S$1,800-S$2,800 | ~S$3,600-S$5,400 |
Actual amounts required will vary, depending on the individual’s lifestyle, but you should budget a minimum of **S$1,800 per month or S$21,600 per year** for living expenses in Singapore. For a fuller picture of what student life really costs, from rent and meals to transport and personal expenses, see the [cost of living in Singapore as an international student](https://mscbiz.nus.edu.sg/blog/insights/cost-of-living-in-singapore-as-an-international-student/).

Financial Aid.content:
Limited Full Scholarship & study awards are available for selected outstanding applicants. Study awards will cover a portion of the programme fees. There is no need to apply separately for the study awards and scholarships, but candidates must submit an application by the [first cut-off date](https://mscacc.nus.edu.sg/admissions/application-process/). Study award and scholarship recipients are chosen based on merit in the following categories:
- **Excellence**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who have done exceptionally well in their academics, as well as during the application process (e.g. interviews).
- **Diversity**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who come from diverse personal and professional backgrounds and experience, and can contribute to the overall experience of their cohort.
- **Resilience**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who have demonstrated determination and resilience to achieve excellence in spite of adversity and hardship.
- **Achievers**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who have achievements in activities outside of the classroom, e.g. promoting or contributing to the UN SDGs; community service in social, environment, or other sectors; entrepreneurship, etc.
- **Local Candidates**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who are Singaporeans or Singapore PRs.
- **ASEAN Candidates**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who are nationals of an ASEAN country.
- **NUS Alumni**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who are NUS Alumni.

Multiple Applications.content: You may apply for up to 5 programmes per admission cycle. An application number will be assigned to you when you create a new online application for each programme. If you are successful in more than one application, you can choose to be admitted to your preferred programme.
